title: Attention Management
equation: Founder Output = Attention Quality × Leverage × Time Allocation
hook: The loudest thing in your inbox is almost never the most important thing in your business.
statement: Spend most of your time on the two or three areas with the biggest payoff.
explainer: Founders spend way too much time reacting to whatever's loudest. But loud doesn't mean valuable. When your attention stays on what actually pays off, momentum builds.
sop: List everything competing for your attention.
Pick the two or three with the biggest payoff.
Block 80% of your deep work for those.
Cut, delegate, or delay the rest.
Score Attention Quality, Leverage, and Time Allocation every week.
equation_example: Attention Quality 7, Leverage 9, Time Allocation 6. 7 × 9 × 6 = 378 Founder Output, out of 1,000. Higher means your hours produce outsized results. Lower means you're busy but the business isn't moving.
question: Name the two or three areas that deserve 80% of your attention right now.
closing_statement: Protect your attention like it's capital.
caption:
Principle Nº 261: Attention Management
